title: Unique Charge-density-wave Order and Fluctuation-induced Phonon Softening in the Optimally-doped Trilayer Cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$
authors: S. Nakata, K. Yamamoto, J. Okamoto, D. Shiga, R. Takahashi, H. Y. Huang, H. Kumigashira, H. Wadati, A. Fujimori, S. Ishida, H. Eisaki, D. J. Huang, J. Miyawaki, H. Suzuki
abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) order is a ubiquitous feature of cuprate superconductors that competes with superconductivity. However, its behavior remains poorly understood in trilayer compounds, which contain the optimal number of CuO$_2$ layers for superconductivity. Here, we report Cu $L_3$- and O $K$-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements of optimally-doped Bi$_{2}$Sr$_{2}$Ca$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{10+δ}$ (Bi2223), the trilayer cuprate with the highest superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) among Bi-based cuprates. We observe CDW order with a single in-plane wavevector of ${\bm q}_{\text{CDW}} = (0.25, 0)$, demonstrating that a coherent CDW order is formed across the trilayers. We also resolve CDW fluctuations emanating from the static order, whose profiles differ between the Cu $L_3$ and O $K$ edges. The phonon softening occurs where these CDW fluctuations interact with the phonon branch, indicating that the RIXS phonon anomaly is driven by the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch.
summary: This work uses RIXS spectroscopy on optimally-doped $	ext{Bi2223}$ to characterize the CDW order, finding it to be coherent across the trilayer structure. Crucially, the study links the observed phonon softening directly to the interaction between the lattice vibrations and the quantum fluctuations associated with the CDW order.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay and competition between Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) order and superconductivity in cuprate superconductors, specifically in the optimally-doped trilayer system.
main_result: They observe a coherent, short-range CDW order across the trilayers and demonstrate that the observed phonon softening is driven by the coupling between these CDW fluctuations and the lattice phonon branch.
method: The primary technique used is Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) performed at both the Cu $L_3$-edge and O $K$-edge.
model_or_system: The physical system is the optimally-doped trilayer cuprate $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Sr}_2	ext{Ca}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{O}_{10+\delta}$ ($	ext{Bi2223}$), which is a high-$T_c$ superconductor. The analysis treats the electronic structure as quasi-two-dimensional.
key_observables: CDW wavevector ($\mathbf{q}_{	ext{CDW}} = (0.25, 0)$), CDW fluctuations, phonon softening (phonon energy minimum), and correlation length ($\xi_a$).
important_parameters: Optimal doping, $T_c = 110 	ext{ K}$, and the distinct probing capabilities of the Cu $L_3$ and O $K$ edges.
main_assumptions: The RIXS phonon anomaly is attributed specifically to the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch, distinguishing it from conventional self-energy effects.
figures_summary: Figures show RIXS intensity maps confirming the static CDW wavevector and resolving phonon/two-phonon excitations, alongside spectral fits detailing phonon dispersion and quasi-elastic intensity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context of CDW/superconductivity competition, details the RIXS measurements at different edges, presents evidence for coherent CDW order across the trilayers, and finally attributes the observed phonon softening to the electron-phonon coupling mediated by CDW fluctuations.
why_interesting: The detailed spectroscopic mapping of coupled electronic and lattice excitations (CDW fluctuations coupling to phonons) provides insights into the underlying pairing mechanism and competing orders in strongly correlated materials, which is relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena.
